End at a certain date, of a plan — Llegar hasta / extenderse hasta.
The schedule goes up to December.
Hand in a test or project — Entregar.
Turn in your essay by Friday.
Reach someone on the telephone — Conseguir hablar con / contactar.
I couldn't get through to the office.
Take someone to where they were before — Llevar de vuelta.
He took us back to the hotel.
Reveal something about yourself by accident — Delatarse / traicionarse.
His trembling hands gave him away.
I hope it all works out for you.
Keep to a belief, habit or plan — Mantenerse en / no apartarse de.

Arrange a date for someone — Buscar pareja a / emparejar.
My cousin fixed me up with her friend.
Go somewhere and leave someone or something there — Dejar atrás.
We left the dog behind with a neighbour.
Take a car or appliance to be repaired — Llevar a arreglar.

Go and see a film, museum or show — Ir a ver / visitar.
We took in a play while we were there.
Take something from one place to another — Llevar.
Take these chairs over to the hall.
Decompose into smaller parts — Descomponerse / degradarse.
Plastic takes centuries to break down.
Force a locked door open — Derribar / echar abajo.
Turn out the lights before bed.
Keep using the same thing — Seguir con / quedarse con.

Be annoyed by what someone did — Molestarse / sentirse ofendido.

Publish or release something — Publicar / sacar.

Do something late that you missed — Recuperar.
He has to make up the exam.
Take an indirect path to avoid something — Rodear / dar un rodeo.
Support someone in a conflict — Respaldar / apoyar.
Be blocked from flowing — Atascarse / embozarse.
